 :Judgment:

This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of 20,00,000/- for the injuries sustained in a Road Traffic accident.

2. The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
That on 10.01.2024 in between 9.00 p.m., to 9.30 p.m., when the Petitioner was riding a motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-42-R-5750 from Channabasappa Circle towards SCCH 15 MVC No.997/2024 MH School side and when he reached near Post O f f i c e , K a n a k a p u r a T o w n , a t t h a t t i m e , o n e m o t o r c y c l e b e a r i n g Reg.No.KA-42-EF-5970 ridden by its rider
came in a rash and negligent manner and with a high speed and dashed against the petitioner's motorcycle.
As a result, the Petitioner fell down and had sustained grievous injuries to all over the body.

Immediately after the accident, the Petitioner was taken to Government Hospital,
Kanakapura and after first aid treatment he was shifted to CDSIMER Hospital,
Bengaluru, wherein the Petitioner took treatment as an inpatient.
He had spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical and other expenses.
Prior to the date of accident, the Petitioner was hale and healthy and he was doing Stationary business and was earning Rs.40,000/- per month.
The said accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-42-EF-5970 by its rider.
The Respondent No.1 is the owner of the offending vehicle and the Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, both SCCH 15 MVC No.997/2024 Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
Hence, this Petition.
3. In pursuance of service of Notice to the Respondents, the Respondent No.1 remained absent and he was placed exparte.
The Respondent No.2 had appeared before the Court through its Counsel and filed its Objection statement to the main Petition.

The Respondent No.2 in its Objection Statement denied the age, avocation and income of the Petitioner and also denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle and also injuries sustained in the said accident.
Further it admitted the issuance of policy in respect of offending vehicle and its validity at the time of accident.
Further it contended that the rider of the motorcycle was not holding valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident.
Therefore, it is not liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
On these grounds, the Respondent No.2 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.

On the rival Pleadings, this Tribunal has framed the following Issues:
ISSUES 1) Whether the Petitioner proves that, he had sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 10.01.2024 between 9.00 to 9.30 p.m., in front of Post Office, Kanakapura Town and Taluk, Ramanagara District, due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-42-EF-5970?
2) Whether the Petitioner is entitled for the compensation as prayed for?
If yes, what is the quantum and who is liable to pay ?
3) What Order or Award?
5. In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 16 documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P-16.
Further he examined one witness as PW.2 and got marked 2 documents at Ex.P17 and 18.
On the other hand, Respondent No.2 did not choose to lead any evidence.

SCCH 15 MVC No.997/2024 6. Having heard the arguments and upon perusal of the depositions, documents exhibited and materials available on record, my answer to the above Issues are as under:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative.

Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per the Final Order, for the following :
REASONS 7. Issue No.1 : It is the case of the Petitioner that, he had sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-42-EF-5970 by its rider.
8. On the other hand, the Respondent No.2 has denied the accident occurred by the rash and negligent riding of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-42-EF-5970 by its rider.

9. In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 16 SCCH 15 MVC No.997/2024 documents at Ex.P-1 to Ex.P-16 and he has re-iterated the Petition averments in his Chief-affidavit.

Ex.P-1 to Ex.P-8 are the True copies of FIR, Complaint,

Upon going through the documents exhibited, Ex.P- 1 & 2 are the True copies of the FIR &
Complaint which shows that on the Complaint lodged by the wife of the Petitioner Smt. Anasuya,
the Kanakapura Traffic Police have registered the case against the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-42- EF-5970 for the offences punishable under Sec.279 & 337 of IPC.
Ex. P.3 & 4 are the true copy of Spot mahazar and Sketch which shows that the concerned police had drawn mahazar and sketch at the spot in the presence of panchas.
Ex.P5 is the Seizer mahazar.
Ex.P.6 is the IMV report which shows that the said accident does not occurred due to any mechanical defects SCCH 15 MVC No.997/2024 of the vehicles.
Ex.P7 is the Wound certificate of the Petitioner.

Ex.P8 is the copy of the Charge sheet which has been submitted by the Sub Inspector of Police, Kanakapura Traffic Police Station against the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-42-EF-5970 for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 337 and 338 of IPC.

Ex.P9 to 16 are the Police Notice and Reply,
Discharge summary, Medical bills, Prescriptions, Aadhaar card, DL and X-rays.

11. Further, the Petitioner has examined doctor by name Dr. Nagaraj B.N as P.W.2 and got marked 2 documents at Ex.P.17 and 18.
12.
PW.1 is subjected for cross examination by the learned counsel for the Respondent No.2.

But,
nothing could be elicited to disbelieve the testimony of PW.1.
The Respondent No.2 did not choose to lead any oral or documentary evidence to substantiate its Objection Statement contentions.
Hence, the Respondent No.2 has failed to substantiate its Objection Statement contentions.

Having regard to the facts and SCCH 15 MVC No.997/2024 circumstances of the case, this Tribunal is of the opinion that the Petitioner has proved the rash and negligent riding of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-42-EF-5970 by its rider and due to the said accident, he had sustained grievous injuries.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 in the 'Affirmative'.
13. Issue No.2:
As the Petitioner has proved that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the offending motorcycle by its rider, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation.
In the Petition, the Petitioner has shown his age as 43 years.
The Petitioner has produced the Aadhaar card and DL at Ex.P14 & 15 respectively shows his date of birth as 10.06.1980.
The accident has taken place on 10.01.2024.
That means, as on the date of accident, the age of the Petitioner was 43 years and 7 months.
Hence, the age of the Petitioner as on the date of accident to be taken at 44 years for consideration.
Further, the Petitioner has averred that, he was doing Stationery business and was earning Rs.40,000/- per month.
But, he has not produced any document in this regard.
Therefore, in the absence of income proof, the notional income to be taken at Rs.16,500/- per month for the purpose of assessment of compensation.

4 With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioner is entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads:
I. COMPENSATION TOWARDS PAIN, SHOCK AND SUFFERING:
15.
The Wound Certificate i.e., Ex.P-7 shows that in the said accident the Petitioner has sustained painful swelling on left wrist.
As per the opinion of the Doctor, said injury is grievous in Nature.
SCCH 15 MVC No.997/2024
Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that, awarding compensation of 20,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.

II. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF AMENITIES :
16.
Bearing in mind the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of 10,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.
III. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF INCOME DURING THE LAID-UP PERIOD:

17. The Petitioner deposed in his evidence that he had taken treatment at CDSIMER Hospital,
Bengaluru.
Upon going through Ex.P.11 - Discharge Summary shows that the Petitioner was admitted as an inpatient in the said hospital from 11.01.2024 to 24.01.2024.
Therefore, while calculating the total period of which the Petitioner was admitted as an inpatient, it comes to 14 days .
SCCH 15 MVC No.997/2024
Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that the laid up period may be considered as two months.

Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of 33,000/- under this head (@ 16,500/- per month ).
IV. COMPENSATION TOWARDS ATTENDANT'S CHARGES, EXTRA DIET & NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE :
18.

Admittedly, the Petitioner had sustained injuries and during the laid up period, the Petitioner might have engaged an attendant and also he might have spent some amount towards extra diet and nourishment and for his conveyance.

In the facts and circumstances of the case, awarding compensation of 6,000/- (@ 100/- per day) towards attendants charges, 6,000/- towards extra diet and nourishment and 6,000/- towards conveyance would be just and reasonable.
In all, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of 18,000/- under this head.

SCCH 15 MVC No.997/2024 V. COMPENSATION TOWARDS MEDICAL EXPENCES :

sentences.text: The Petitioner has stated in his evidence that, he had spent huge amount towards medical expenses.
In order to prove this fact, he has produced medical bills at Ex.P12 totally amounting to Rs.20,413/-.
I have gone through the same and the same is acceptable.
Hence, by rounding off the same, the same to be taken at Rs.20,420/-.
Hence, I am of the opinion that the Petitioner is entitled for Rs.20,420/- under this head.
VI. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS / COMPENSATION TOWARDS PERMANENT DISABILITY:
20. The Petitioner has stated that due to the injuries sustained by him in the accident, he has suffered permanent disablement and he is not able to do his work as he used to do earlier.
Even in his evidence, P.W.1 has deposed to that effect.

21. Further, the Petitioner got examined Dr. Nagaraj B.N as P.W.2 who has deposed regarding the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in a Road Traffic Accident and the SCCH 15 MVC No.997/2024 treatment taken by him.
Further, he assessed the physical disability of the Petitioner towards Left arm at 39% and towards whole body disability at 13%.
PW.2 got marked Clinical notes and X-ray at Ex.P17 and 18.
In the cross- examination PW.2 admitted that the Petitioner had sustained only one injury and the same was cured.
He further admitted that the Petitioner did not sustain compound fracture.

Having regard to the medical records placed on record, the evidence of P.W.2 and the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that considering the disability of the Petitioner with respect to the whole body at 4% would be just and proper.
22. As per Sarla Verma's Case (2009 ACJ 1298 SC), the multiplier applicable to the Petitioner is 14.

With multiplier of 14, income of 16,500/- per month and disability of the Petitioner with respect to his whole body at 4%, the loss of future income comes to 1,10,880/- (16,500/- x 12 = 1,98,000/-,
1,98,000/- x 14 x 4/100 =1,10,880/-).
Hence, SCCH 15 MVC No.997/2024 the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of 1,10,880/- under this head.

TOTAL COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLED:
23.

To sum up, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
1. Pain, shock & Suffering  20,000/-
2. Loss of amenities  10,000/-
3. Loss of income during the laid up  33,000/-
period 4.

Thus, totally the Petitioner is awarded compensation of 2,12,300/- with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of this petition till the date of realization.

Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent riding on the part of the riding of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-42-EF-5970.
There is no dispute about the validity of the Policy at the time of the accident.
In this case, the Respondent No.1 is the owner and Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, the Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to satisfy the award amount.
The Respondent No.2, who is liable to indemnify the Respondent No.1, has to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 is "Partly in the Affirmative".
25. Issue No.3:

In view of my findings on Issues No. 1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the U/S 166 of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.

SCCH 15 MVC No.997/2024  The Petitioner is entitled for  Compensation of 2,12,300/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.
The Respondent No.2 being the insurer, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.
Out of the compensation amount awarded to the Petitioner, 75% of the award amount with accrued interest shall be released to the Petitioner by way of E- payment and after proper identification.
The remaining 25% award amount shall be deposited as F.D. in the name of the Petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled bank for a period of three years.
